voice.name: Carl - Steady Storyteller
voice.description: Matured male voice with calm depth and measured pacing, perfect for narrations and documentaries
voice.note: Public Cartesia stock voice; not a clone of any real person.

beats.narration: Lisa, when I was little, my dad Paul gave me my own corner of his workbench. I built Heathkit electronics and took apart whatever he brought home.
Taking the leap was terrifying. But my friend Woz and I built the Apple I in my parents' garage in Los Altos.
The moment that changed everything was when you came to live with me as a teenager, and I finally got to be your dad up close.
Lisa, the Lisa computer was named after you, and I should have said so sooner. You can't connect the dots looking forward. Stay hungry. Stay foolish.

A shot from a feature-quality 3D animated film, production CG, RenderMan global illumination. Lighting: Warm golden-hour late afternoon daylight streaming through window, soft warm bounce, dusty air motes.

[CAMERA AND PERFORMANCE]

Action: A young child actively engaged in their childhood world, immersed in the memory of building Heathkit electronics and taking apart whatever my dad brought home

[ANIMATION RULES]
Motion: everything winds the opposite way before it moves. Heads and hands travel in gentle curves and arcs, never robotic straight lines. Fast between key poses with a subtle organic overshoot on arrival that settles naturally. Hair and cloth arrive a beat after the body and keep moving a beat past the stop. Every held pose is an organic moving hold with gentle breathing, small weight shifts, and natural blinks. Ground contact has physical weight transfer.
Eye life: continuous micro-saccades, living asymmetric catchlights, natural blink rate, eyes dart to target before the head turns.
Performance: face stays completely honest and sincere; no exaggerated mugging or cartoon pantomime.
